I'll tell my story as it happened. On October 31st, my puppy Rocky (an English bulldog) was picked up. From the moment they arrived, the person who picked him up had absolutely no idea how to put a dog in the carrier. Although he didn't want to go in, they're supposed to have trained personnel for these kinds of situations. Not all dogs will go in willingly. From the start, things went wrong. They had to carry him on the ground, tied to the door, because there was no other option (I agreed). He left very tense because of the whole time (1 hour) they spent trying to get him in. That same evening, they sent me photos and a video showing him "calm" (at this point, I don't know if they sedated him to relax him; the video they sent me gave me that impression). The next day, they told me he was "better" in the morning, but in the videos and photos, he wasn't reacting; he seemed out of it. I decided to leave him with them while I was traveling, and on Friday they contacted me to say he was unwell. Because of work, I couldn't answer right away. When I finally got back to them, they said, "He's not well. We gave him an IV to keep him from deteriorating," but he's still not well. That afternoon, I decided to go back because something told me he wasn't okay. The distance and the bus trip meant it took me all afternoon to get there. I went to where they keep him, a ranch near the Teotihuacan pyramids. When I arrived, they wouldn't let me in. They left me waiting outside for about 10 minutes. When they finally came out, two people were carrying my puppy on a bed. I picked him up, spoke to him, but he didn't react. The person who attended to me refunded me the full amount, saying his health came first (at this point, I feel like it was remorse and a way of distancing themselves from what would happen, so they would have an excuse to say they hadn't been paid or something like that). I took my puppy to a nearby vet because he had blood in his nose. When we arrived (it was a 24-hour clinic), the vet said he had a possible case of poisoning from something he ate or some medication that was administered incorrectly. I told him the whole story, and when he checked his paw (where they had put the IV fluid), he said they hadn't even inserted it properly. All the fluid had stayed in his paw because it was swollen. They gave him medication for the possible poisoning and IV fluids, but the vet said it would take a few hours because his eyes were red and the veins on his tongue were very prominent. When he moved his tongue, he vomited, and I could smell digested blood in his vomit. They inserted an IV, and he stayed at the vet all night. Around 4:00 a.m., he had a bloody bowel movement from his rectum. By 6:30 a.m., he went into crisis and suffered cardiac arrest. His body couldn't take it anymore; he had internal bleeding everywhere. The truth is, I don't know what happened to him. He was perfectly healthy, not overweight, and had no other health issues. I handed him over in good condition, and they returned him to me almost dead. I have no proof, but I also have no doubt that he wasn't treated well. The fact that the vet who examined them didn't know how to administer an IV drip speaks volumes and leaves much to be desired. I firmly believe that life gives back everything, good and bad. Today, I'm still grieving for my puppy and saddened by what happened. I hadn't written before because I wanted to take the time to avoid writing from a place of anger and resentment. I reiterate, life itself takes its toll, and if they did something wrong, I hope they remember Rocky when life makes them pay. If it's the first time your dog or pet has been left outside, think twice before leaving them here. Pay attention to the signs if they don't want to leave. Today, I regret letting him go when he didn't want to, and especially believing that everything was fine when I saw him "calm." I tell my story from what happened to me and how it was, nothing more and nothing less, just what was. I hope my comment is helpful and that it isn't deleted.
